**Quick answer:** a finished one-bedroom condo on Isla Verde sold for a median of 180,000 CRC in the first half of 2026, transfer costs add 3.5% on top, and a clean title transfer takes 21 days from deposit to registration. This guide walks through the numbers, the fees and the order of steps.

## What a condo costs in 2026

Prices depend on the district and the age of the building more than on the view. The table below uses the median asking price per square metre for the four districts we track.

| District | Median price per sqm | Typical unit |
|---|---|---|
| [Playa Norte](/areas/playa-norte/) | 2,400 CRC | 55 sqm one-bedroom |
| [Playa Sur](/areas/playa-sur/) | 1,900 CRC | 62 sqm one-bedroom |
| Puerto Viejo | 1,450 CRC | 70 sqm two-bedroom |
| Cerro Alto | 1,100 CRC | 85 sqm two-bedroom |

A new building in Playa Norte is roughly twice the price of a ten-year-old building in Cerro Alto for the same floor area. Buyers who need a rental income usually pick the coast, buyers who plan to live on the island pick the hills.

## Fees at completion

Transfer costs are paid by the buyer unless the contract says otherwise. Expect four lines on the closing statement.

| Fee | Rate | Who pays |
|---|---|---|
| Transfer tax | 1.5% of the declared price | buyer |
| Registry stamp | 0.5% | buyer |
| Notary | 1.0% capped at 4,000 CRC | buyer |
| Agent commission | 3% plus tax | seller |

On a 180,000 CRC purchase the buyer pays about 6,300 CRC in taxes and notary fees. Budget another 1,200 CRC for the lawyer who reads the building's minutes and checks the debt position of the owners' association.

## Pros and cons of buying new versus resale

New buildings come with a five-year structural warranty and lower service charges in the first two years. Resale units in older buildings cost less per square metre and let you read three years of association accounts before you commit.

The cons run the other way. A new building can slip six to nine months past the promised handover date. An older building can carry a special assessment for the roof or the lifts that the seller does not mention.

## Risks and what to check before you sign

The three checks that matter are the title certificate from the registry, the association's debt statement and the building permit that matches the unit you are buying. A missing permit is the one defect that cannot be fixed after purchase.

According to the Isla Verde Statistics Office, gross rental yield on one-bedroom coastal condos averaged 5.1% in 2025 across the four districts, so any listing that promises more should show you its own booking history rather than a projection.

## Scenarios: who this guide is for

Scenario one is the remote worker who wants a base for eight months a year and rents the unit out for the rest. A 55 sqm one-bedroom within 15 minutes of the marina fits that job. Scenario two is the family buying a two-bedroom in Cerro Alto to live in, where the school run is the deciding factor and the [district comparison](/guides/dup-b/) matters more than the yield.

## Step by step: from offer to keys

**Step 1:** reserve the unit with a deposit of 5,000 CRC, refundable for 14 days.

**Step 2:** the lawyer pulls the title certificate and the association debt statement within 7 days.

**Step 3:** sign the purchase contract and pay 10% of the price.

**Step 4:** the notary registers the transfer and you receive the keys, usually 21 days after the deposit. For the documents you will need, read the [document checklist](/guides/dup-c/) and the [Marina Towers card](/projects/marina-towers/) if you are buying in that building.

## Frequently asked questions

**Q: Can a foreigner own a condo outright on Isla Verde?**

Yes. Condominium units are registered in the buyer's own name with no residency requirement. Land under a detached house follows a different rule, covered in the [land ownership guide](/guides/dup-a/).

**Q: How long does the title transfer take?**

Three weeks is the norm when the seller's paperwork is complete. It stretches to two months when the association debt statement is disputed.
